issues.title: [P2][Steward] One-time evidence-backed backlog burn-down for upstream families and obsolete bot reports
issues.author: mbtiongson1
issues.body:
## Baseline (2026-10-22)
- 221 open repository issues.
- 105 open issues authored by `github-actions[bot]`.
- 96 open `upstream:child` intakes across four umbrellas: #1835 (72), #2002 (17), #2020 (4), #1823 (3).
- 6 open release umbrellas; one additional open bootstrap (#2091).
- `gh-aw` leftovers #2126 (aggregated threat-detection issue) and #2127 (Copilot org billing failure) need separate evidence-based disposition now that the GitHub agentic workflows were paused.
- Other genuine feature/curation issues are **not** to be mass-closed for a clean-looking counter.

## One-time migration / operational pilot
1. Generate a **read-only exhaustive inventory** grouped by parent issue/upstream source and prior merge/approval state. Verify that results include all pages and complete body payloads.
2. For each candidate, establish whether a canonical skill is already present and correctly curated; whether a version sync PR has landed; whether a child was formally rejected; whether a prior issue already preserves its work; or whether it's still actionable.
3. Partition into **A** provably resolved/superseded/duplicate, **B** independently-curatable/repairable batch, **C** founder decision. Do not equate stale age or `skip-child-gate` with approval/rejection.
4. After the reviewed reconciliation engine is in place, **close only eligible A issues with linked proof** and preserve relevant information in canonical parent/ledger. Batch real B work by suite using Haiku default + independent verification, consistent with the current one-dispatch-per-run limit. Compress C to concise founder questions.
5. Review obsolete `gh-aw` bot issues individually: close resolved infrastructure failures only if the failing automation is verifiably disabled and an explicit supersession/closure reason applies; preserve any independent security concern.
6. Rerun the watcher in dry-run mode to ensure closed issues do not immediately reappear; adjust source emission as needed **before** bulk closure.
7. Publish before/after census, closure/PR links, unresolved B/C count, no-loss audit and recurrence test. Stop on ambiguity.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Per-family report for all 96 child tickets; zero silent drops of valid intake candidates.
- [ ] Demonstrable decline in *unresolved issue noise* without inflating a hidden unreviewed backlog.
- [ ] A closure receipts contain exact parent, PR/registry proof, and closure reason.
- [ ] B cases progress through normal Steward budgets; C compresses into bounded founder review.
- [ ] Second pass is idempotent: no accidental reopen/duplicate/recreation storm.
- [ ] Complete daily/weekly summary includes open-issue net change and new/repeated bot noise.

This issue is a **one-time sweep** after the deterministic reconciler and upstream-emission fix; do not create a new standing queue or automatically classify upstream candidate acceptance from lack of activity.

issues.title: [P1][Upstream] Stop child-issue fanout and coalesce release/candidate noise before GitHub issue writes
issues.author: mbtiongson1
issues.body:
## Problem
`.github/workflows/upstream-watcher.yml` polls **daily with `--apply`**. `scripts/upstream_watcher/issuer.py` currently generates one umbrella plus an individual issue per `componentAdds` entry. This is intentional under `docs/agents/upstream-watcher.md` §F3 but is generating an unmanageable queue: **96 open auto-generated upstream children**, distributed as **72 under #1835, 17 under #2002, 4 under #2020, and 3 under #1823**. Current `skip-child-gate` approvals do not dispose of open children. The watcher already updates an umbrella in place on newer releases; that is worth preserving.

## Programmatic reduction, before any LLM
- Treat GitHub issues as **exceptions requiring action**, not one per observed candidate. Stage all upstream delta/candidate data in stable, typed, deduplicated batch payloads attached to the suite/umbrella and Steward ledger.
- Compare each proposed candidate with canonical registry IDs, existing intake work, prior accepted/rejected dispositions, tracked upstream release versions, renamed/aliased skills and PR history **before issue emission**. Do not claim semantically identical solely by title/slug.
- Define an idempotent per-suite/release key and enforce one active actionable canonical object. Preserve all per-candidate evidence, attribution and original source URLs. Coalesce repeated version churn into existing umbrella; avoid comment spam and resetting approvals invisibly.
- Replace or heavily constrain **automatic child fanout** with one **batch review** containing independently addressable rows. Generate a separate child only when an actionable row genuinely requires its own tracked decision after deterministic prechecks or Class B curation.
- Avoid unbounded approval bypass: explicit `skip-child-gate` must not silently mean 'accepted' or 'close every child'. Make family transitions explicit and lossless.
- Validate the **policy change** against §F3 (which currently rejects a single consolidated issue). Present a narrow founder decision before changing that approved contract. Do not silently rewrite prior intake semantics.
- Feed structured observations into the existing Steward A/B/C disposition mechanism rather than opening separate bot policy pathways. Fail closed on watcher/network errors; no issue creation on unknown evidence.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Dry-run simulation on the four real backlog families shows proposed new issue count, suppressed duplicates, and retained candidate evidence.
- [ ] Zero lost candidate records, no false admissions, no high-volume issue fanout from a re-run of the same release.
- [ ] Explicit founder-compatible F3 policy amendment/review for new emission semantics.
- [ ] Test idempotency, pagination/index eventual-consistency, racing watcher runs, newer-release updates and approved/rejected paths.
- [ ] The daily watcher produces a compact suite status/Steward observation; issues are created only for unresolved actionable exceptions.
- [ ] Reconciliation cannot auto-dismiss ambiguous Class C candidate decisions.

References: #1835, #2002, #2020, #1823; `scripts/upstream_watcher/issuer.py`; `docs/agents/upstream-watcher.md` §F3.

issues.title: [P1][Steward] Deterministic GitHub issue reconciliation, A/B/C classification, and proof-based closure
issues.author: mbtiongson1
issues.body:
## Problem
Steward observes local upstream drift but does not reconcile GitHub issue lifecycle. Live audit (2026-10-22): **221 open issues**, **96 open `upstream:child` intakes**, **6 `upstream:release` umbrellas**, **105 open issues authored by `github-actions[bot]`**. Issues keep accumulating despite existing watcher issue creation/dedup and close-on-reject workflows.

The Steward operating model already requires semantic deduplication by unresolved condition, final dispositions with receipts, and a compressed founder desk (see `founder/STEWARD-OPERATING-MODEL.md` §§4–6,12). Implement this **as an atomic Steward capability**, not another competing bot queue.

## Design: deterministic first
- Ingest **all pages** of relevant GitHub issue/PR state, tracked watcher payloads, upstream→umbrella→child links, registry named-skill state, canonical CLI outcomes, and merged PR provenance; fail visibly on permission, pagination or freshness gaps.
- Produce a machine-readable **read-only dry-run reconciliation manifest** with stable semantic keys, evidence, current state, proposed `A/B/C` disposition, and expected issue transition.
- Distinguish **resolved**, **superseded**, **duplicate**, **actionable**, **awaiting founder**, **not evaluated** and **ambiguous**. Stale ≠ resolved.
- Proposed **Class A (narrow, policy-controlled)**: close only where deterministic evidence proves exact merged/current-version resolution, accepted/rejected child disposition, or lossless duplicate/supersession into a still-tracked canonical item. Verify canonical slug/provenance and preserve original payload/links in closure receipts. This is a **new issue-write authority**: codify and review its precise allowlist before enabling writes, never infer permission from existing unrelated Class A sensors.
- **Class B:** any real semantic review, candidate mapping, intake, release reconciliation or nontrivial code changes. Batch bounded work by upstream suite and dispatch via existing Haiku builder + independent verifier, not issue-by-issue agents.
- **Class C:** governance/ambiguous classification, trust, rejected-vs-accepted judgments without existing authority; produce one decision packet per actual founder question, referencing all affected tickets.
- Execute idempotently: re-read issue/PR and registry at action time, compare against expected snapshot, apply closure reason and comment with linked proof, checkpoint per issue/group, retry safely; never delete issues. Leave unresolved tickets open.
- Keep receipts including before/after census, reasons, closure URLs, unknown coverage and failure details. No new issue per run.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `gaia steward`-compatible observation / triage / disposition contract with fixture tests, stable keys and durable receipts.
- [ ] Reproduce counts and classify sampled umbrella/child groups (#1835, #2002, #2020, #1823), including `skip-child-gate` and partial integration states.
- [ ] Dry run emits a complete paginated reconciliation matrix and no mutations.
- [ ] Class A closure requires explicit, reviewed policy allowlist and hard proof; fails closed on incomplete evidence.
- [ ] B/C route into existing bounded agent lane/founder desk, no new orchestration platform, no API billing dependency.
- [ ] Executed pilot is replay-idempotent; receipts prove eligible issues closed and ambiguous/unreviewed intakes preserved.
- [ ] Daily `/gaia-steward-full` can invoke this atomic capability without more than the established dispatch budget.

Related: #1580 (prior upstream sensor governance gap, closed), #2001 (Steward rhythm), #1922 (curation correctness).

issues.body:
This issue tracks all runs where threat detection flagged problems in agentic workflows in this repository. Each workflow run that completes with a detection warning or failure posts a comment here.

<details>
<summary>What is a Detection Problem?</summary>

A detection problem occurs when the threat detection system either:

- **Detects potential security threats** (prompt injection, secret leak, malicious patch)
- **Fails to produce results** (agent failure, parse error)

Comments distinguish `threat_finding`, `detector_execution_failure`, `detector_result_invalid`, and `detection_outcome_unknown` using the structured detection reason. Detector failures leave the security assessment incomplete; they do not prove a threat or a clean result. Comments omit agent text and detection payloads.

When `continue-on-error: true` (the default), these problems produce warnings and safe outputs still proceed. When `continue-on-error: false`, they block safe outputs entirely.

</details>

<details>
<summary>How This Helps</summary>

This issue helps you:

- Track workflows where threat detection raised concerns
- Review patterns of detection warnings or failures
- Identify false positives or recurring issues with threat detection
- Monitor the health of the threat detection system

issues.author: mbtiongson1
issues.body:
## Context
PR #2119 introduced Gaia Steward Full: 30 registered detectors, 46 bindings across 17 maintenance routines. Registration and fixture tests do not establish that each detector is executing against real repository inputs. Founder requests this as a **separate follow-up issue**, not an addition to the pending Sonnet activation prompt.

## Scope
- Inventory all 30 detectors and 46 bindings from `founder/steward/routine-coverage.json`, with owning routine(s), declared inputs, scan triggers, authority class, and remediation routing.
- Verify real scheduled invocation and per-detector execution against the actual repository. Provide durable per-detector receipts showing observed, not-evaluated, unavailable/unknown, or partial-coverage states. Never infer healthy from absent or skipped evidence.
- Supply and validate the three driver inputs where supported: `test-history` (`.gaia/steward/inputs/test-history.json`), `ci-health` (`.gaia/steward/inputs/ci-runs.json`), `dependency-advisory` (`.gaia/steward/inputs/advisories.json`). Record freshness, repository identity, and blockers; do not fabricate input data.
- Produce an operational coverage matrix separating **activation coverage** (executed with valid inputs), **detection coverage** (remaining blind spots for each of 17 routines), and **repair readiness** (Class A executor, Class B dispatch/independent verifier, Class C founder escalation, or report-only/unrouted).
- Ensure findings flow to debt ledger and established A/B/C authority paths when configured; do not broaden mutation authority or automatically change canonical Trust/governance records.
- Clearly document remaining semantic coverage gaps (e.g. incident learning, rendered browser accessibility, external usage evidence, cross-version schema compatibility). Do not call a partially covered routine complete.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] All 30 registry detectors and 46 bindings are accounted for in a machine-readable matrix.
- [ ] Real run IDs/receipts prove which detectors executed with valid inputs and identify missing/stale inputs or skipped subjects individually.
- [ ] The three driver-input dependencies have working provenance/freshness validation or explicit blockers.
- [ ] Findings and debt/authority routing are reconciled with the executed scans, including unrouted Class B debt.
- [ ] Each of 17 routines lists measured detector coverage and remaining blind spots without false 100% claims.
- [ ] Documentation explains how to reproduce the operational report and check it after activation.

## Separation of work
Track this independently of the founder-approved Sonnet mission to merge and activate the Steward automation. Do not block that mission solely on broader semantic-coverage work in this issue. References: #2119, #2114.

issues.title: [P1] Curation safety minimum: no candidate loss, authentic L4, replay-safe batch handoff
issues.author: mbtiongson1
issues.body:
## Goal
Fix the **proven invariants**, not build a full orchestration engine. Applies equally to inference-first Opus curation and assisted Luna/Flash curation.

## Audit-confirmed defects
- PR #2089: forged local L4 metadata and fabricated/empty receipt accepted at packet-to-intake seam; **NO MERGE** until independent human authority is verified.
- Candidate IDs such as `synthetic/a-b` and `synthetic/a/b` can resolve to same packet filename and silently overwrite a candidate.
- Valid packet batch alone does not establish the expected candidate inventory was complete.
- Live generic snapshot validation varies by submission branch; prefill can claim exact dedupe without running it.
- Repeated submissions can generate new time-derived batch IDs; preserve existing intake IDs/receipts.

## Minimal repair
1. Close L4 approval forgery for **exact reviewed payload and revision**, with verified human authority independent of agent-editable text. Fail closed on missing/stale proof; keep genuine outside-top-K human mappings possible. Approval remains required for BOTH lanes.
2. Collision-resistant candidate persistence, explicit ownership and safe failure.
3. Lightweight batch accounting: every expected candidate exactly one of review-ready, deferred, rejected or proven duplicate. Six named skills mapped to one generic remain six rows. No giant fan-out runtime.
4. Consistent fresh current-catalog validation, truthful exact-dedupe status, and content-derived idempotent submission/continue-existing-intake behavior.
5. Preserve merged #2093 lowercase/collision protections and immutable Actions handoff/recovery semantics. Keep #2088 as owner of broader multi-packet implementation; align changes rather than duplicate its scope.

## Verification, proportional to risk
Targeted synthetic negative tests for forgery, empty receipt, changed payload, slash/hyphen collision, missing candidate, shared generic identities, stale catalog, and replay; one small-batch and one suite walkthrough. Independent Luna review. Do not repeat a large broad proving campaign just to justify batching.

## DoD
Focused code/skill fixes and regression evidence on a PR, independent review, clear separate verdict for #2089 (**NO MERGE remains until repaired and approved**). No real curation/intake mutation, automated promotion, or merge. Related: #2088, #1644, #1691.

issues.title: [P1] Lean curation: Scout Core, inference-first fast lane, assisted low-inference lane
issues.author: mbtiongson1
issues.body:
## Goal
Make curation **easy for one founder-curator**, not a general-purpose orchestration product. Reduce prompts, hops, redundant tools and tokens while preserving Gaia's canonical outputs.

## Working model
- **Scout + Curation Core** own discovery context, candidate interpretation, overlap/generic mapping, evidence proposals, and review presentation.
- **Fast/high-inference lane** (e.g. Opus): reason directly over sources and compact suite inventory; use only essential tools. A complete batch should not require a new orchestration engine.
- **Assisted/low-inference lane** (Luna/Flash): use deterministic tool supports, explicit prefill/dedup/provenance and bounded fan-out as needed. Extra tools compensate for lower inference, not add approval authority.
- Same outcome contract for both: preserve each named skill, generic topology, provenance and evidence claims; exact candidate accounting; one concise human review surface; canonical CLI changes only after authorization.
- **All existing L4, evidence, calibration and merge gates stay enabled.** Potential future fast-lane gate changes are *out of scope and not approved*.

## Sol-led execution
Sol High leads by reading/inference, defines small bounded tasks, integrates. **Luna owns ~85% of the investigation, edits, tests and independent reviews.** Astra Max is an optional read-only advisor for hard architectural ambiguity, called sparingly by Sol only. Explicit thinking level for every invocation. No other models without founder permission.

## Smallest useful work
1. Inspect Scout and Curation Core, then chain/dynamic/full-pipeline skill routing and overlap. Confirm real behavior versus documentation.
2. Classify each tool/step **keep / simplify / optional for assisted lane / remove / fix**; quantify friction where cheaply observable, otherwise give reasoned qualitative assessment.
3. Produce one compact curator UX for *single skill* and *12-skill suite* (candidate inventory → suggestion/justification → one L4 review → canonical intake/evidence). No mandatory full state machine.
4. Implement only minimal demonstrated improvements; no speculative framework or exhaustive new testing campaign. Reuse #1644 for typed tools and #1691 for mode-specific execution proof, without expanding them automatically.
5. Demonstrate that Opus-class fast lane can use a compact source/inventory/decision bundle; Luna lane may use stricter deterministic helpers. Record any remaining manual founder step.

## DoD
Short before/after friction comparison; working instructions/compact manifest or targeted tooling PR; no loss of named identities; unchanged canonical governance. Cross-reference #1644, #1691, #2088 and PR #2089. No merge, promotion, or gate relaxation without separate founder approval.

issues.title: Spike: explore Pi Durable for Gaia Steward Class B incident workflows
issues.author: mbtiongson1
issues.body:
## Skill Tree examples
- Trust/ranking drift and stale evidence: capture reproducible invariant violations and provenance.
- Meta-sweep continuation after interruption without contaminating canonical evidence.
- Failed checks or preview parity: investigate and prepare scoped repair proposals without unsolicited changes.

## Goal
Explore Pi Durable as an optional local, recoverable execution layer for Steward's existing Class B incident workflow. This is an exploratory spike, not a commitment to adoption.

## Candidate use cases
- One durable execution per incident: detection, investigation, remediation proposal, explicit authorization checkpoint, execution, tests, verification, closure.
- Local scheduled/event-driven triage as an alternative to cloud routines, with zero model calls when idle.
- Crash/restart recovery without losing prior investigation and without duplicating GitHub issues, branches, PRs, or external writes.
- Persistent human handoff: a concise record of evidence, proposed action, approval status, cost, and next step.
- Deduplicate repeated incidents, but retain independent audit trails.
- Continue to use the current Pi agent/subagent tooling for coding; evaluate Durable as a separate orchestration adapter, not a replacement.

## Research questions
- Compare Pi Durable versus a minimal SQLite-backed job queue and scheduler, including no-adoption.
- Verify support and limitations for SQLite persistence, resumption, tool integrations, Node.js/Termux operation, scheduling, context compaction, usage accounting, and hard budget enforcement.
- Decide how execution checkpoints coexist with the existing authoritative Steward incident ledger.
- Test incident recovery at investigation, authorization-pending, tool execution, and verification phases.
- Measure tokens, cost, idle CPU, memory, storage, and failure/duplicate rates.
- Keep explicit model + thinking-effort selection, user-authorized model tier/agent dispatch, no unapproved fanout, and no Pi subagent turn cap. Enforce independent scope, safety, and spend gates.

## Non-goals and safeguards
No immediate production deployment, repo rewrite, automatic remediation, merges, unauthorized dispatch, or changes to existing Steward detection. Read-only by default; any implementation, mutation, or deployment follows current approvals and test/preview gates. Protect secrets and sensitive data. Design for optional disable/rollback.

## Suggested exit criteria
A short architecture decision, a small opt-in isolated prototype if justified, crash/recovery and idempotency demonstration, cost comparison, risks, and a go/no-go recommendation.

issues.title: fix(meta): make meta sweep re-appraise evidence, trust, and rank
issues.author: mbtiongson1
issues.body:
## Summary

Hardens the mirrored `gaia-meta-sweep` skill contract after the Jev dogfood run in #2031 exposed an orchestration failure: the agent exercised Jev/intake/issue modes instead of performing the canonical current-tree sweep.

This patch keeps Jev, Luna, and deterministic Gaia machinery in their proper layers.

## What changes

- Defines a **non-negotiable completion gate** for a real meta sweep.
- Makes the canonical subject the complete **post-ingest current tree**, not the intake backlog.
- Adds a first-class **Appraise** phase for every in-scope named skill:
  - canonical evidence inventory
  - deterministic Trust Magnitude / Overall Trust Grade via `scripts/trust_appraise.py --skill ...`
  - current rank vs evidence-backed rank eligibility
  - Origin / Champion review when ordering changes
- Requires a coverage receipt: named skills, generic nodes, evidence rows, all 13 dimensions, Jev calls/fallbacks, and proposed deltas.
- Integrates Jev into the fan-out for semantic questions:
  - `--mode evidence` for evidence meaning / methodology concerns
  - `--mode meta` for generic abstraction / vendor-neutrality review
- Routes ambiguous or consequential semantic cases to Luna.
- Preserves deterministic authority for liveness, Trust arithmetic, grades, rank gates, Origin / Champion rules, and all mutations.
- Explicitly prevents issue triage, upstream triage, intake mapping, Jev demos, or single-node reviews from being reported as a completed meta sweep.
- Prevents provider instructional-skill installation from being treated as a dependency of the workflow.
- Requires the report to say `FULL META SWEEP COMPLETE` only when the completion gate is satisfied; otherwise it must say `PARTIAL META AUDIT`.

## Core invariant

> **Jev judges meaning; Gaia computes authority.**

Jev is now a semantic reviewer *inside* the sweep, not the sweep itself.

## Files

The two mirrored copies are byte-identical:
- `.agents/skills/gaia-meta-sweep/SKILL.md`
- `.claude/skills/gaia-meta-sweep/SKILL.md`

## Context

#2031 is being retained/repaired as the Jev advisory-lane dogfood and triage artifact it actually represents. This PR repairs the skill contract before the next actual sweep is run.

issues.title: Steward Upgrade - Curation
issues.author: mbtiongson1
issues.body:
Summary

Gaia's curation pipeline is getting good at finishing large intake batches, but we do not yet have enough independent evidence that the semantic curation itself was correct, nor a reliable guarantee that a newly admitted skill leaves curation with a visible evidence state.

The current upstream integration batch makes the gap concrete. Lane 02 escalated 31 difficult rows; after stronger independent review and maintainer adjudication, 8 of those 31 final dispositions changed (~26%). That proves the second review layer adds value. It does not prove the remaining non-escalated rows were correct, because they did not receive the same adversarial treatment.

There is a second failure mode: a curator may correctly admit a skill, land it in the registry, and then move on before meaningful evidence is gathered. The skill looks "done" even though its evidence array is empty, source-only, weak, stale, or otherwise below the level we would want to investigate later.

This issue adds Curation Assurance under Gaia Steward: four independent sensors plus a mandatory evidence-closure contract. The goal is not to replace human/maintainer governance or make every admission expensive. The goal is to make semantic uncertainty, evidence debt, and later curation corrections visible and measurable instead of disappearing after merge.

Doctrine

upstream/discovery candidate
        ↓
primary curator
        ↓
curation assurance
  ├─ independent disagreement
  ├─ semantic overlap / novelty
  ├─ outcome feedback
  └─ random audit
        ↓
evidence closure gate
        ↓
clean | evidence-search debt | Class C disagreement
        ↓
verified intake / later evidence campaign

Steward should continue to own detection, debt, priority, authority, deduplication, and receipts. Curators propose canonical meaning. Assurance sensors observe whether the proposal has enough independent support to deserve trust or further governance review.

These sensors must not automatically mutate canonical curation. Disagreement is evidence, not authority.

Sensor 1 — Independent Curation Disagreement

Run a shadow curation pass that cannot see the primary curator's answer.

Inputs should include only the material legitimately available to an independent reviewer:

- release-pinned / canonical source "SKILL.md"
- relevant existing named skills
- relevant generic skills / retrieval candidates
- current curation rubric and policy
- upstream/source attribution metadata

Compare at least:

- disposition: "accepted | mapped | deferred | omitted"
- proposed mapping target / "genericSkillRef"
- named-vs-suite-vs-standalone placement where applicable
- proposed star entry level
- transferability / repo-local judgment
- topology-impact flags

The shadow reviewer must not inherit the first curator's rationale or disposition.

Emit normalized disagreement observations such as:

- "curation_disposition_disagreement"
- "curation_mapping_disagreement"
- "curation_placement_disagreement"
- "curation_level_disagreement"

Material disagreement is Class C / maintainer-review debt, never an automatic correction.

The 2026-09-23 upstream batch showed that 8/31 escalated decisions changed after stronger review. We need to capture this systematically rather than relying on whether a curator happened to mark "ESCALATE".

Sensor 2 — Semantic Overlap / Novelty

For every "accepted" candidate, and preferably every "mapped" candidate, retrieve the strongest existing semantic neighbors.

This sensor does not decide the mapping. It produces an adversarial evidence packet asking whether the curator's novelty claim survives contact with the nearest alternatives.

Flag patterns such as:

- accepted despite very strong overlap with an existing named skill
- accepted despite an existing generic/named implementation that appears to subsume it
- mapped despite weak similarity to the selected target
- omitted despite apparently high semantic distance from existing skills
- new generic proposed when an existing generic appears adequate
- suite component admitted as standalone, or standalone admitted as suite-only, without explicit rationale

Use deterministic retrieval snapshots and record model/version metadata when semantic search or reranking is involved.

Related: #1675.

Possible findings:

- "curation_novelty_low"
- "curation_mapping_similarity_low"
- "curation_generic_overlap"
- "curation_placement_overlap"

These are review signals, not canonical decisions.

Sensor 3 — Curation Outcome Feedback

Build the missing longitudinal feedback loop.

For previously curated skills, detect later events that imply the original curation required correction:

- accepted → later mapped/consolidated
- mapped → later admitted as distinct
- omitted/deferred → later admitted
- generic target changed
- suite/standalone placement corrected
- duplicate later discovered
- installability/source attribution corrected
- evidence rejected or removed
- admission reverted
- topology changed because the original abstraction was wrong
- repeated maintainer override of the same curator/rubric pattern

Record these as outcome labels suitable for an oracle/eval set.

At minimum measure:

- disposition agreement rate
- adjudicator overturn rate
- false-accept proxy rate
- false-omit proxy rate
- mapping-target correction rate
- placement correction rate
- escalation precision
- escalation recall once random auditing exists
- evidence-closure rate
- evidence-quality improvement rate after admission

Do not rank individual humans or models publicly from tiny samples. This is a system-quality instrument first.

Our own curation history should gradually become the best labeled eval set for Gaia curation.

Sensor 4 — Random / Stratified Audit

Do not review only the rows that the primary curator marked uncertain.

A confident error is more dangerous than an escalated one.

Default policy proposal:

- 100% of "accepted" rows creating new named skills
- 100% of new generic/topology decisions
- 100% of explicit "ESCALATE" rows
- 100% of unusually high proposed entry levels
- stratified random 15–25% sample of "mapped" and "omitted" rows
- optional contributor/source-family sampling so one large upstream cannot dominate the audit set

Sampling must be deterministic from a recorded seed/batch ID so a curator cannot influence which rows receive review.

The random sample lets us estimate whether the escalation mechanism itself misses bad decisions.

Every audited row records:

- primary decision
- independent decision
- agreement/disagreement dimensions
- adjudicated result if reviewed
- sampling reason
- source snapshot
- evidence state at time of audit

Mandatory cross-cutting guard — Evidence Closure

A curation pass is not silently finished merely because the skill entered the registry.

Every newly accepted named skill must leave the curation pipeline with an explicit evidence state.

This is intentionally fail-visible, not universally fail-closed. If current policy permits a valid low-star skill to land without independent evidence, it may still land. What must become impossible is losing track of that evidence debt.

Evidence states

Normalize at least:

1. none — no evidence rows
2. source-only — upstream/repository pointer establishes provenance but not independent quality
3. weak/unverified — candidate evidence exists but has not passed verification
4. verified — at least one eligible evidence item has passed verification
5. independent — at least one meaningful own-layer independent witness exists
6. strong/reproducible — benchmark/verifier/peer-review or equivalent high-quality evidence appropriate to current policy

Exact names can align with the G7 taxonomy, but the distinction between source provenance and independent quality evidence must remain explicit.

Evidence debt queue

Steward should answer mechanically:

«Which named skills exist today with no evidence, source-only evidence, weak evidence, stale evidence, or evidence below their current star/Trust expectations?»

Emit debt such as:

- "evidence_missing"
- "evidence_source_only"
- "evidence_unverified"
- "evidence_quality_low"
- "evidence_stale"
- "evidence_grade_mismatch"

This feeds a deduplicated evidence-search queue that can be handed to research agents later.

A founder should be able to run something equivalent to:

gaia steward evidence-queue

and receive:

- skill ID
- current stars / Trust grade
- current evidence state
- evidence types already present
- missing witness class
- last evidence verification date
- source/upstream pointer
- why the item is queued
- suggested evidence-search objective

No agent should have to rediscover which skills were admitted during a busy sprint and never received evidence.

Evidence quality, not just presence

A nonempty "evidence[]" must not automatically clear the queue.

The guard must distinguish:

- source/provenance from evaluation
- same-author/self-claims from independent witnesses
- popularity/proxy metrics from implementation-specific evidence
- live evidence from dead/stale evidence
- verified evidence from merely valid URLs
- duplicated evidence from genuinely independent origins
- evidence supporting the actual named skill from evidence supporting only its upstream repository or generic capability

Reuse existing machinery:

- "EvidenceLinkHealthSensor"
- "BenchmarkFreshnessSensor"
- Trust calibration / G7 gates
- #1671 evidence-curation queue

The higher-level question is:

Does this skill have enough useful evidence, and if not, is that debt visible?

Curation Confidence Receipt

Every curated batch should leave a machine-readable receipt. Do not rely on model self-reported confidence.

Per candidate:

candidate
primary disposition
primary mapping / placement
source snapshot
nearest semantic alternatives
independent disposition, when audited
disagreement dimensions
adjudicated outcome
evidence state
evidence debt kind(s)
topology impact
sampling reason

Batch receipt should summarize:

- accepted / mapped / deferred / omitted
- audited count and sampling rate
- disagreement count
- adjudicator changes
- unresolved Class C rows
- accepted skills with no evidence
- accepted skills with source-only evidence
- accepted skills with verified independent evidence
- evidence-search queue additions

This becomes durable eval material for future curator/model routing.

Steward authority

Finding| Class
missing evidence state / malformed receipt| A/B depending on repairability
evidence missing / source-only / stale| B research debt
weak semantic-overlap warning| B observation; C if canonical change proposed
independent curation disagreement| C
mapping / topology disagreement| C
random-audit disagreement| C
evidence quality requiring promotion/demotion| existing G7/human-verifier gate

A stronger model may investigate or prepare a richer packet. It must not gain canonical mutation authority because it is stronger.

Suggested implementation phases

P1 — Contract + historical audit

- define Curation Confidence Receipt schema
- add explicit evidence-state vocabulary
- scan the current registry and produce the first evidence-debt inventory
- identify all named skills with zero / source-only / weak evidence
- connect existing #1671 work rather than duplicating it
- backfill recent curation batches where enough provenance exists

Deliverable: founder-visible list of skills that landed but still need evidence.

P2 — Independent disagreement + random audit

- implement shadow-curator packet generation
- deterministic stratified sampling
- disagreement debt
- no canonical mutation
- build an oracle fixture from the 2026-09-23 batch, including the 31 escalated rows and the 8 changed final dispositions

P3 — Semantic overlap / novelty

- integrate deterministic retrieval/reranking
- emit nearest alternatives and novelty warnings
- reuse #1675 evaluation work where possible
- keep mapping decisions human-gated

P4 — Outcome feedback

- derive correction labels from later registry/timeline/history changes
- publish rolling curation-quality metrics
- feed adjudicated outcomes back into the oracle set

P5 — Evidence research dispatch

- Steward produces bounded evidence-search packets
- research agents may discover candidate evidence
- all ingestion still goes through "/ev-pipeline" / verifier gates
- research agents cannot self-promote stars or Trust grades

Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The four curation-assurance sensors are specified and wired through Steward debt/receipt semantics.
- [ ] Primary and independent curator outputs are isolated.
- [ ] Random auditing covers confident decisions, not only explicit escalations.
- [ ] A registry-wide report identifies every named skill with missing, source-only, weak/unverified, stale, or insufficient evidence.
- [ ] Newly accepted named skills cannot leave curation without an explicit evidence state.
- [ ] Lack of independent evidence remains visible debt even when policy allows the skill to land.
- [ ] Evidence presence and evidence quality are separate concepts.
- [ ] Evidence-search debt is deduplicated and can generate bounded research-agent prompts.
- [ ] Existing EvidenceLinkHealth / BenchmarkFreshness / G7 verification logic is reused rather than forked.
- [ ] The 2026-09-23 upstream batch becomes an initial oracle fixture, including the 8/31 escalated decisions changed after adjudication.
- [ ] Curation outcome corrections can be measured over time.
- [ ] No assurance sensor automatically changes canonical disposition, mapping, topology, stars, Trust grade, or evidence.
- [ ] Founder/verifier gates remain intact.

Related

- #1477 — Gaia Steward doctrine and maintenance-debt control plane
- #1644 — tool-assisted curation orchestration
- #1664 — governed Steward sensor fleet
- #1671 — evidence curation queue
- #1675 — stronger semantic matching / retrieval eval
- #1908 / #1915 — 2026-09-23 upstream integration batch

issues.title: TM Index (2026 Q3) — Branch-aware TM formula rebuild (G8, blocked by Yggdrasil II)
issues.author: mbtiongson1
issues.body:
**Parent EPIC:** Follow-through to Yggdrasil II (separate EPIC — to be created)
**Ratification handover:** `founder/handovers/YGGDRASIL_II_RATIFICATION_2026-07-07.md` § Follow-through
**Blocked by:** Yggdrasil II staging→main merge

## Scope

Rebuild the Trust Magnitude formula to be **branch-aware**, fixing the fusion-scoring inflation/deflation for Uniques identified during the Yggdrasil II ratification interview (Q10).

## The bug

TM Index (2026 Q2) (= G7) fusion-recipe weight (1.5×) and sqrt-softening (`200 + 20 × sqrt(origins − 10)` past 10) were engineered for **suites**. Under Yggdrasil II:

- A Unique that happens to live inside a suite (`suiteRef` present, generic `suiteComponents` absent) inherits fusion signal it did not structurally earn — inflated TM.
- A genuinely-standalone Unique (`suiteRef` absent) scores lower than merit warrants because the fusion-recipe row is either missing or zero-weighted — deflated TM.

## Deliverable — branch-aware TM formula

- **Suite branch**: current TM formula preserved (sqrt-softening, 1.5× fusion-recipe weight)
- **Unique branch**: fusion-recipe rows contribute 0. TM scored purely from non-fusion evidence types, with re-weighting favoring `peer-review` (currently 1.2×), `benchmark-result` (currently 1.4×), and social-signal / adoption evidence. New Unique-specific weight: `depth-of-integration` proxy (proposed)
- **Standard branch (1★–3★)**: current formula unchanged

## Downstream

- All 43 4★ named skills + 5 5★s will be regraded against the new formula after Yggdrasil II migration lands. Grade churn expected.
- Leaderboard at `/trust/leaderboard/` reflects new scores post-regrade.
- Handover doc: `founder/handovers/TM_INDEX_2026_Q3_RATIFICATION_<date>.md` when this RFC lands.

## Public naming

- Public docs: **TM Index (2026 Q3)**
- Internal codename: **G8**
- Predecessor: TM Index (2026 Q2) = G7

## Non-goals

- No Yggdrasil III schema changes (that would be a separate Meta Schema RFC)
- No touching the Apex Gate predicates directly (only the TM inputs that feed them)
